articles.summary: Warm weather remains a leading draw for prospective homebuyers considering a move in retirement, but family connections are playing an equally important role among those already retired, according to a new PulteGroup survey of 1,330 prospective homebuyers at or nearing retirement age. Among respondents who are still working and considering an out-of-state move, 62% chose weather and climate as one of their top two reasons, followed by affordability and cost of living at 47% each and proximity to family or friends at 35%. Among those already retired, however, family connections carried greater weight. Forty-five percent of retired respondents considering an out-of-state move selected proximity to family or friends, tied with weather and climate as the leading considerations. While the survey does not track how individuals’ priorities change over time, it reveals differences in what working and retired prospective buyers emphasize when considering an out-of-state move. articles.title: Beyond Sunshine: New PulteGroup Survey Highlights What Matters Most to Homebuyers in Their Next Chapter
